drhp.business: Jenburkt Pharmaceuticals is engaged in the manufacture and marketing of pharmaceutical formulations in India, with its therapeutic identity built on the downstream consequences of diabetes and related chronic conditions — neuropathy, musculoskeletal complications and cardiovascular morbidity. Its brands Nervijen, Cartisafe Forte and Powergesic are positioned to serve the patient pool expanding around these chronic-disease categories, including the GLP-1-driven growth in anti-diabetic therapy.
drhp.expansion: The company acquired an industrial plot at Sihor and procured analytical equipment (UPLC, FTIR, Dissolution Tester, Stability Chambers and related instrumentation) to strengthen R&D and quality-testing infrastructure; the Sihor R&D unit is also where Powergesic Natura Oil, the Pharma India Vertical's first phyto-therapeutics product, was developed. Separately, management describes a planned field-force expansion into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities this year to capture chronic-care consultation volumes that are growing faster than in metro centres.

risks.note: Government permits only a 0.64% price revision on scheduled drugs for FY2026-27, structurally capping realisations unless the company shifts mix toward differentiated, non-NLEM formulations.
risks.risk: Drug price control (DPCO/NLEM) on scheduled drugs

risks.note: Growing international presence, increasing digitalisation of operations and heightened global cyber threats prompted management to maintain a dedicated Cyber Liability Insurance Policy alongside conventional business-liability cover.
risks.risk: Cyber security and data protection exposure

risks.note: Company had to undertake a comprehensive review and restructuring of employee compensation (PF applicability/wage limits, ESIC compliance) to align with the revised statutory wage-code framework.
